name: What image formats can I convert to PDF?

acceptedAnswer.text: PDFree supports JPG/JPEG, PNG, and WebP. Each image becomes one page in the output PDF.

name: Is there a file size limit?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. PDFree has no file size or image count limits.

name: Will the image quality be reduced?

acceptedAnswer.text: By default, PDFree compresses images slightly (JPEG quality 82%, capped at 2400px on the longest side) to keep the PDF a reasonable size — visually almost unnoticeable. Turn off "Compress images" before converting if you need the exact original resolution.

name: Can I mix JPG and PNG images in one PDF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Add any combination of JPG, PNG, and WebP files. Each becomes a page in the final PDF regardless of format.

name: What page size will the PDF use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each page is sized to exactly match its source image's pixel dimensions at 96 DPI. A 2480×3508 image (A4 at 300 DPI) produces a standard A4-sized page.

name: Is there a limit on how many images I can convert?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Add as many images as you need. Processing time scales with total image size — dozens of photos may take 10–20 seconds on slower devices.

name: Does the tool upload my images anywhere?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. All processing happens in your browser using the pdf-lib JavaScript library. Images are loaded into browser memory and never transmitted.

name: Does PDFree store or log my files after processing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. PDFree runs entirely in your browser — there is no backend server that receives your files. Because nothing is uploaded, nothing can be stored, logged, or retained. Your document exists only in your browser's memory for the duration of the session and is cleared when you close the tab.
